title: The prayer of the righteous reaches him, and the riches of the unrighteous flow away like water
summary_md: The chapter opens on the day the woes come due, and Enoch sets the two ends side by side so the righteous can hold on: *Believe, ye righteous, that the sinners will become a shame And perish in the day of unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:1). What turns that day is not the strength of the righteous but their prayer, which is heard: *And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach unto Yahuah (Lord), And for you the days of your judgement shall come.* (1 Enoch 97:5). The men who built their lives on gathered silver hear the same verdict James will preach centuries later: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: ‘We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), and then the answer, *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). James heard the same cry rising from the reaped fields: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, cries: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The Psalm had already drawn the two roads, the one that prospers and the one that perishes: *For Yahuah (LORD) knows the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). The righteous do not win the day by force. They pray, the prayer is heard, and what was gathered in unrighteousness runs off like water.
note: old quotes 97:17-18 were invented (the two-ways charge lives in ch 91/94); rebuilt on the live 97:1-10 — prayer heard, riches flow away; new title; Deut 30 and Psalm 1:1/1:3 dropped, Psalm 1:6 and James 5:4 added from the index

title: All your deeds are written down in heaven
summary_md: Enoch takes away the one thing the oppressor counts on, that nobody sees. *I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, by the Holy Great One, That all your evil deeds are revealed in the heavens, And that none of your deeds of oppression are covered and hidden.* (1 Enoch 98:6). He will not let them talk themselves out of it either: *And do not think in your spirit nor say in your heart that ye do not know and that ye do not see that every sin is every day recorded in heaven in the presence of the El Elyon (Most High).* (1 Enoch 98:7), *From henceforth ye know that all your oppression wherewith ye oppress is written down every day till the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 98:8). The canon keeps the same ledger, and it records both sides of the page. Malachi saw the righteous written in: *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16). Later in the same book Enoch answers the sinner who says the record will never be kept: *And, although ye sinners say: “All our sins shall not be searched out and be written down,” nevertheless they shall write down all your sins every day.* (1 Enoch 104:7). James says the fraud of the rich is already in the ears of heaven: *the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth* (James 5:4). Nothing done to the poor is lost. It is written the day it is done, and the book waits for the day of judgement.
note: 104:9 'books of the living opened' was invented; replaced with the live 104:7 (sins written down every day); 98:7 re-quoted in full

title: Fear not, ye souls of the righteous — wait for the day of judgement
summary_md: When the fire comes, Enoch asks the sinners a question they cannot answer: *In those days when He hath brought a grievous fire upon you, Whither will ye flee, and where will ye find deliverance? And when He launches forth His word against you Will you not be affrighted and fear?* (1 Enoch 102:1). The whole creation shakes before that word, *And ye sinners shall be cursed for ever, And ye shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 102:3). Then he turns to the dead who died keeping the covenant, and the tone changes entirely: *Fear ye not, ye souls of the righteous, And be hopeful ye that have died in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 102:4), *And grieve not if your soul into Sheol has descended in grief, And that in your life your body fared not according to your goodness, But wait for the day of the judgement of sinners And for the day of cursing and chastisement.* (1 Enoch 102:5). Wisdom says the same thing about the same souls: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). The world reads their death wrong — *In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:2) — *but they are in peace* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:3), *their hope full of immortality* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). The righteous dead are not forgotten in Sheol; they are told to wait, because a day is coming that settles the account. Daniel names who comes out of it: *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). They were written before they died. The day only reveals it.
note: 102:3 'souls of the righteous in the hand of Elohim' is Wisdom 3:1, not Enoch; rebuilt on live 102:1-5 (fear not, be hopeful, wait); Wisdom and Daniel kept; title adjusted

title: As we die, so die the righteous — the sinners' taunt over the dead, and its answer
summary_md: Enoch lets the sinners say their piece over the graves of the righteous, and it is the oldest taunt there is: *And yet when ye die the sinners speak over you: ‘As we die, so die the righteous, And what benefit do they reap for their deeds?* (1 Enoch 102:6), *Behold, even as we, so do they die in grief and darkness, And what have they more than we? From henceforth we are equal.* (1 Enoch 102:7), *And what will they receive and what will they see for ever? Behold, they too have died, And henceforth for ever shall they see no light.’* (1 Enoch 102:8). The whole argument rests on the grave being the end, and the canon answers it at the grave itself. Daniel was shown the awakening: *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3), and Yahusha (Jesus) set the same shining at the harvest: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.* (Matthew 13:43). Wisdom stages the very scene Enoch records, with the mockers now watching the man they mocked: *This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:3), *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:4), *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:5). Malachi heard the same complaint in his own day, *It is vain to serve Elohim (God)* (Malachi 3:14), and showed the book that settles it: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* (Malachi 3:16). The sinners counted themselves equal with the righteous dead because both went into the ground. The book of remembrance says otherwise, and the day of awakening reads it out.
note: 102:7 'righteous shining like the sun' was invented; rebuilt on the live taunt 102:6-8 answered by Daniel 12, Matthew 13:43, Wisdom 5, Malachi 3 (all kept); new title

title: Content to eat and drink and acquire wealth — whither will ye flee from the fire?
summary_md: Enoch puts one question to the men who lived for their table and their takings: *In those days when He hath brought a grievous fire upon you, Whither will ye flee, and where will ye find deliverance? And when He launches forth His word against you Will you not be affrighted and fear?* (1 Enoch 102:1). He describes their life without any ornament: *I tell you, ye sinners, ye are content to eat and drink, and rob and sin, and strip men naked, and acquire wealth and see good days.* (1 Enoch 102:9). Against that he sets the end of the righteous, who had none of it and did no violence to get it: *Have ye seen the righteous how their end falls out, that no manner of violence is found in them till their death?* (1 Enoch 102:10). Yahusha (Jesus) names where that fire ends: *And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 13:42). Malachi saw the same day with its two sides: *the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble* (Malachi 4:1), while *unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings* (Malachi 4:2), and he closes the whole prophecy with *Remember ye the law of Moses my servant* (Malachi 4:4), because the Torah is what still stands on the far side of the oven. The Psalmist had already told the poor man not to be moved by what the rich man gathered: *Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;* (Psalm 49:16). The good days Enoch's sinners saw were real, and so is the fire. The question of where to flee from it has no answer for a man whose whole life was the eating and the acquiring.
note: 102:17-22 (kings, gods, 'where are your riches now') do not exist in Charles; rebuilt on live 102:1, 102:9-10; Matthew 13:42, Malachi 4, Psalm 49 kept; new title

title: The oath: the spirits of the righteous dead shall live and rejoice
summary_md: Enoch does not merely hope this; he swears it, and he says where he read it. *Now, therefore, I swear to you, the righteous, by the glory of the Great and Honoured and* (1 Enoch 103:1) *Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you. I know a mystery And have read the heavenly tablets, And have seen the holy books, And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them:* (1 Enoch 103:2), *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3), *And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:4). That is the resurrection hope the canon carries in the same words. Daniel saw the awakening: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2), and the wise *shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever* (Daniel 12:3). Yahusha (Jesus) sealed it: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father* (Matthew 13:43). And the wisdom of the fathers said it plainly, *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (The Wisdom of Solomon 3:1), *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality* (The Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). What Enoch read on the heavenly tablets is what Daniel was shown and what the King spoke in the open. The righteous dead are kept, their memorial is kept, and they will live.
note: 103:4 and 103:7 were quoted from the corrupt text; the oath lives at live 103:1-4 and is quoted there in full; canon witnesses kept

title: Written in the holy books — the lot of the righteous dead, and the names that are blotted out
summary_md: Enoch's assurance to the righteous rests on something he read, not something he guessed. *Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you. I know a mystery And have read the heavenly tablets, And have seen the holy books, And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them:* (1 Enoch 103:2), *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3). Their lot is written before they die, and their memorial does not go out with them: *And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:4). Malachi saw the same book being kept: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16), and John saw it opened at the end: *another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works* (Revelation 20:12), with the rest promised to the ones written there: *Blessed are the dead which die in Yahuah (Lord) from henceforth... that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them* (Revelation 14:13). Enoch's last book tells which way the pen moves on that page. Names are never added late; they are blotted out: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3). The righteous were written before the Great One from the start. What the end does is keep the name or strike it.
note: 103:2-3 quotes were invented ('books of life', 'names written'); rebuilt on live 103:2-4 (holy books, lot written, memorial kept) and 108:3 (blotted out); canon kept; title adjusted

title: Blessed are the sinners, they have seen all their days — and then Sheol
summary_md: Enoch lets the sinner's friends preach his funeral, because the sermon is the lie itself: *Woe to you, ye sinners, when ye have died, If ye die in the wealth of your sins, And those who are like you say regarding you: “Blessed are the sinners: they have seen all their days.* (1 Enoch 103:5), *And now they have died in prosperity and in wealth, And have not seen tribulation or murder in their life; And they have died in honour, And judgement has not been executed on them during their life.”* (1 Enoch 103:6). Then he tells them what the grave actually holds: *Know ye, that their souls will be made to descend into Sheol And they shall be wretched in their great tribulation.* (1 Enoch 103:7), *And into darkness and chains and a burning flame where there is grievous judgement shall your spirits enter; And the great judgement shall be for all the generations of the world. Woe to you, for ye shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 103:8). Yahusha (Jesus) told the same story about a man who died in honour and prosperity: *And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom* (Luke 16:23), *I am tormented in this flame* (Luke 16:24). Revelation gives the end of it for the name not found in the book: *And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire* (Revelation 20:15). None of this is cruelty for its own sake. It is requital, measured to the deed, as Enoch had already said to the man who wronged his neighbour: *Woe to you who requite your neighbour with evil; For ye shall be requited according to your works.* (1 Enoch 95:5). The man who died with judgement never executed on him in his life has not escaped it. He has only postponed it to the one place he cannot buy his way out of.
note: 103:6 and 103:10-11 were invented; rebuilt on live 103:5-8; Luke 16, Rev 20:15 kept, 95:5 from the mechanical re-quote kept; title adjusted

title: They helped those who robbed us — the rulers who sided with the oppressor
summary_md: The righteous bring their complaint to Enoch, and it is the complaint of every generation that has been eaten alive by the men who were supposed to protect it: *We desired to get away from them that we might escape and be at rest, But found no place whereunto we should flee and be safe from them.* (1 Enoch 103:13), *And we complained to the rulers in our tribulation, And cried out against those who devoured us, But they did not attend to our cries And would not hearken to our voice.* (1 Enoch 103:14), *And they helped those who robbed us and devoured us and those who made us few; and they concealed their oppression, and they did not remove from us the yoke of those that devoured us and dispersed us and murdered us, and they concealed their murder, and remembered not that they had lifted up their hands against us.* (1 Enoch 103:15). Enoch had already pronounced the woe on the men at the top of that table: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). The prophets and the brother of Yahusha (Jesus) sound the same alarm, and it is aimed at the heaping of land and treasure and the defrauding of labourers, not at persons. Isaiah: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place* (Isaiah 5:8). James: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1), *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth* (James 5:4). The rulers in Enoch's chapter would not hear the cry. James says it went past them and was heard anyway. The wisdom of the fathers gives the oppressor's own verdict on the far side of it: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (The Wisdom of Solomon 5:8).
note: CHECK found a second invented quote the grader missed ('103:15, 24' riches shall not endure); rebuilt on the live anchor 103:13-15 (the complaint to the rulers) with 96:5 and the canon witnesses kept; new title

title: Two lots in one chapter: the righteous dead rejoice, the prosperous sinner goes down to Sheol
summary_md: The whole of this chapter is built on two lots, and Enoch swears to both. To the righteous: *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3). To the sinner who died rich and honoured, with judgement never executed on him in his life: *Know ye, that their souls will be made to descend into Sheol And they shall be wretched in their great tribulation.* (1 Enoch 103:7). Between the two he records the complaint of the righteous in this life, and the words they use are the words of the exile curse: *We hoped to be the head and have become the tail: We have toiled laboriously and had no satisfaction in our toil; And we have become the food of the sinners and the unrighteous, And they have laid their yoke heavily upon us.* (1 Enoch 103:11). That is the Torah's own fork, and Moses set it before the people in the same two words: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same two roads: *For Yahuah (LORD) knows the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). And the wisdom of the fathers shows where the road of the righteous comes out: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High* (The Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). The righteous in Enoch's day felt like the tail. The lot written for them says they are not, and the way of life that leads there is the Torah itself, never the curse.
note: 103:25 (two paths charge) does not exist; the chapter's own two lots (103:3 / 103:7) with the righteous' exile-language complaint (103:11) carry the thread; Deut 30, Psalm 1:6 (index), Wisdom 5:15 kept; new title

title: Ye shall shine as the lights of heaven — companions of the hosts of heaven
summary_md: Enoch swears to the righteous that heaven has not lost track of them: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1). Then he tells them what their shame turns into: *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2), *Be hopeful, and cast not away your hope; for ye shall have great joy as the angels of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:4), and the company they are headed for: *And now fear not, ye righteous, when ye see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for ye shall become companions of the hosts of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:6). Daniel was shown the same shining on the far side of the grave: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), where *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). Yahusha (Jesus) names the same hope at the harvest: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). And the Wisdom of Solomon sees the persecuted righteous vindicated in the same light: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). The shining is not something the righteous work up in themselves. Their names were already written before the glory of the Great One; the day of their visitation only makes visible what heaven already had on record.
note: the mechanical re-quote had swapped in 50:2, which does not carry the shining; live 104:1-2, 104:4, 104:6 do; canon kept; title adjusted

title: Your names are written before the glory of the Great One — blotted out, never added
summary_md: Enoch puts the register first and the shining second: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1), *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2). The name is on the page before the man is vindicated, not after. That is the canon's book of remembrance: *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* (Malachi 3:16). Daniel ties the deliverance to the same book: *and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.* (Daniel 12:1). And scripture only ever speaks of the pen moving one way on that page. Names are blotted, never written in late: *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.* (Psalm 69:28), which Yahusha (Jesus) confirms to the overcomer, *He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.* (Revelation 3:5). Enoch's last book says the same of the wicked: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3). The ones who hear were already written. The warning about the blot is spoken to them, not to those who were never on the page.
note: 104:3 and 104:8 were invented; the live 104:1 carries 'your names are written before the glory of the Great One'; 108:3 quoted in full; canon kept; title adjusted

title: Every sin written down — and the sinners who alter the words and write their own books
summary_md: Enoch answers the sinner who thinks the record is never kept: *And, although ye sinners say: “All our sins shall not be searched out and be written down,” nevertheless they shall write down all your sins every day.* (1 Enoch 104:7), *And now I show unto you that light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins.* (1 Enoch 104:8). Then he names the sin that will do the most damage to the generations after him, the handling of the words themselves: *And now I know this mystery, that sinners will alter and pervert the words of righteousness in many ways, and will speak wicked words, and lie, and practise great deceits, and write books concerning their words.* (1 Enoch 104:10). Over against those books he sets the ones written truthfully: *But when they write down truthfully all my words in their languages, and do not change or minish ought from my words but write them all down truthfully—all that I first testified concerning them.* (1 Enoch 104:11), *Then, I know another mystery, that books will be given to the righteous and the wise to become a cause of joy and uprightness and much wisdom.* (1 Enoch 104:12). The Torah had already drawn that line around its own words: *You shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall you diminish ought from it, that you may keep the commandments of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) which I command you.* (Deuteronomy 4:2), and Jeremiah watched the scribes cross it: *How do you say, We are wise, and the law of Yahuah (LORD) is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain.* (Jeremiah 8:8). The books that are written down every day and the books that were altered both come to the same table at the end: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12), where *whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.* (Revelation 20:15). The verdict is not arbitrary. The record was kept the whole time, and the men who rewrote the words of righteousness are in it.
note: 104:9/104:12 'books of the living opened' were invented; the live anchor 104:9-12 is about sins written daily and sinners altering the words / books given to the righteous; built on 104:7-8, 104:10-12 with Deut 4:2 and Jer 8:8 added from the index; Rev 20 kept; new title

title: The sinners growing strong and prospering — keep afar from their violence
summary_md: Enoch does not pretend the sinners are losing in this life. He tells the righteous what to do while the sinners are winning: *And now fear not, ye righteous, when ye see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for ye shall become companions of the hosts of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:6). The woe he had already laid on that prospering says how it was got and how it ends: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: ‘We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Isaiah cried the same woe against the men who swallowed the land a field at a time: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!* (Isaiah 5:8). James turns it on the hoarders of the last days: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.* (James 5:1), for *the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The woe is on the taking and the treading, on the system that wrings wealth out of labourers, and not on persons as such. And the chapter ends with the other recompense, the one that waits for those who kept apart from it: *And to them shall the books be given, and they shall believe in them and rejoice over them, and then shall all the righteous who have learnt therefrom all the paths of uprightness be recompensed.’* (1 Enoch 104:13).
note: 104:14-24 do not exist; the woes live at 96:5 / 97:8 (kept from the re-quote) and the anchor 104:13 is the recompense of the righteous; built around 104:6; Isaiah 5:8 and James kept; new title

title: The books given to the righteous teach the paths of uprightness
summary_md: Enoch does not end this chapter with a father's charge in his own words; he ends it with the books. *Then, I know another mystery, that books will be given to the righteous and the wise to become a cause of joy and uprightness and much wisdom.* (1 Enoch 104:12), *And to them shall the books be given, and they shall believe in them and rejoice over them, and then shall all the righteous who have learnt therefrom all the paths of uprightness be recompensed.’* (1 Enoch 104:13). The paths of uprightness are learned from the books, and the books are the ones written down without change, as he had just said: *But when they write down truthfully all my words in their languages, and do not change or minish ought from my words but write them all down truthfully—all that I first testified concerning them.* (1 Enoch 104:11). That is Moses setting the two ways before the people out of the same written word: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), pressed to its choice, *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter frames the same fork, *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:6). The way of life is a written way, and the Torah is that writing. The righteous who learn the paths of uprightness from it are the ones Enoch says will be recompensed, which is the same thing the King said of the man who does and teaches the least of its commandments: *Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:19).
note: 104:25 (two-paths charge) does not exist; live 104:11-13 carries 'the paths of uprightness' learned from the books; Deut 30 and Psalm 1:6 kept, Matthew 5:19 added from the index; title adjusted

title: I and My Son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness
summary_md: The Epistle ends with the Father speaking, and he does not speak alone: *In those days Yahuah (Lord) bade (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) unto them; for ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 105:1), *For I and My Son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness in their lives; and ye shall have peace: rejoice, ye children of uprightness. Amen.* (1 Enoch 105:2). Read that slowly. The One speaking has a Son, and the two of them together are joined to the children of uprightness for ever. David heard the same voice speak to the same Son: *I will declare the decree: Yahuah (LORD) has said unto me, You are my Son; this day have I begotten you.* (Psalms 2:7), and the Son himself said what the union amounts to: *And this is life eternal, that they might know you the only true Elohim (God), and Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), whom you have sent.* (John 17:3). The children of uprightness are known by name before any of this, which is why they can be told to rejoice before the day comes. Malachi saw the book that holds those names: *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16), and Daniel ties the deliverance to it, *at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). The Father and the Son walking with their own in the paths of uprightness is the whole of the covenant said in one sentence, and the Torah is the path they walk it on.
note: 105:1-2 quotes were invented and the prose was degraded; chapter 105 is two verses and the live 105:2 names the Father and the Son united with the children of uprightness — built on that, Psalm 2:7 and John 17:3 added from the index, Malachi 3:16 / Daniel 12:1 kept; new title

title: Ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth
summary_md: The last word of the Epistle sets the righteous over the earth, not as its owners by conquest but as its guides: *In those days Yahuah (Lord) bade (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) unto them; for ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 105:1). That is the inheritance the Psalter promised to the ones who waited rather than grabbed: *For evildoers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon Yahuah (LORD), they shall inherit the earth* (Psalm 37:9), *The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever* (Psalm 37:29). Yahusha (Jesus) set it as a beatitude, *Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth* (Matthew 5:5), and Daniel saw the kingdom handed to the same people: *And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the El Elyon (most High), whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him* (Daniel 7:27). The office they hold over the whole earth was named at Sinai: *And you shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.* (Exodus 19:6). This is no church standing in for Yashar'el (Israel). It is the covenant seed, the children of uprightness, set as guides to the children of earth in the reign, and the land-promise of the Torah stands under it. They did not earn the earth; they waited on Yahuah (God) and were kept, and at the end they are told to rejoice.
note: 105:3 ('righteous shall inherit the earth') does not exist; live 105:1 sets the righteous as guides and recompense over the whole earth; Psalm 37, Matthew 5:5, Daniel 7:27 kept, Exodus 19:6 added from the index; new title

title: Show it unto them — the wisdom of the righteous as a light to the children of earth
summary_md: When the Epistle closes, the righteous are not told to hide their light and wait; they are sent: *In those days Yahuah (Lord) bade (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) unto them; for ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 105:1). The wisdom shown to the children of earth is the light the prophets saw rising on the gathered: *Arise, shine; for your light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon you.* (Isaiah 60:1). Daniel ties the shining to exactly this work of guiding others: *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever* (Daniel 12:3), after *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2). Yahusha (Jesus) said the same two things to the same people, that they will shine in the kingdom, *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father* (Matthew 13:43), and that they are to be seen now: *You are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.* (Matthew 5:14), *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 5:16). Isaiah promises the dust will give back the ones who shine: *Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead* (Isaiah 26:19), and the Wisdom of Solomon sees the same sparks: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). The names were written first. Then they wake, they shine, and they show the children of earth the wisdom they were given.
note: 105:4 ('shine as the lights of heaven') lives at 104:2, not 105; this thread is built on the live 105:1 charge to show wisdom to the children of earth, with Isaiah 60:1 and Matthew 5:14,16 added from the index; Daniel, Matthew 13:43, Isaiah 26:19, Wisdom 3:7 kept; new title

title: Ye shall have peace — the end of the refrain that gave the sinners none
summary_md: All through the Epistle one line keeps falling on the sinners like a hammer: ye shall have no peace. The last verse of the Epistle turns the same word the other way and gives it to the righteous: *For I and My Son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness in their lives; and ye shall have peace: rejoice, ye children of uprightness. Amen.* (1 Enoch 105:2). Isaiah had the same refrain and the same division: *There is no peace, says Yahuah (LORD), unto the wicked.* (Isaiah 48:22), *There is no peace, says my Elohim (God), to the wicked.* (Isaiah 57:21). What stands between the two peaces is the day, and the Epistle's whole hope rests on that day coming. Isaiah saw it: *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire* (Isaiah 66:15), *For by fire and by his sword will Yahuah (LORD) plead with all flesh: and the slain of Yahuah (LORD) shall be many* (Isaiah 66:16). Paul binds it to the revealing of Yahusha (Jesus): *And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Yahusha (Lord Jesus) shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels* (2 Thessalonians 1:7), *In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not Elohim (God), and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ)* (2 Thessalonians 1:8). And the canon says plainly whose prophecy that coming was: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints* (Jude 1:14). The judgement falls on the ungodly for what they have done, not on persons for being persons, and on the far side of it the children of uprightness are told to rejoice, because the peace is theirs and the Father and the Son are with them.
note: 105:5-6 (Most High arises in wrath) do not exist; chapter 105 ends on 'ye shall have peace' — built on that against Isaiah 48:22/57:21 (index) with the day of Isaiah 66, 2 Thess 1, Jude 14 kept; new title

title: He will comfort the earth after all the destruction — Noah, the sign of what is coming
summary_md: Lamech was afraid of the child, and Enoch's answer travels back down through Methuselah with two things in it: the boy is his, and the boy is a sign. *And now, my son, go and make known to thy son Lamech that this son, which has been born, is in truth his son, and that (this) is no lie.’* (1 Enoch 107:2), *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). The name itself is the promise, given before the flood it answers. Genesis names the grace that stood behind it: *But Noah found grace in the eyes of Yahuah (LORD)* (Genesis 6:8), *These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with Elohim (God)* (Genesis 6:9), and the verdict is spoken over him face to face, *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation* (Genesis 7:1). The choosing comes first and the keeping follows it. Elohim (God) saw the righteous one before the water rose and carried him through it, and the keeping is never a wage paid afterward for merit. Jubilees says the same of the one house: *no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways* (Jubilees 5:19). What Enoch read on the tablets reaches past Noah's own flood: *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1). The child who comforted the earth after one destruction is the sign of the generation that comes after the last one.
note: 107:5 was invented; built on the live 107:1-3 (the name Noah, 'comfort the earth after all the destruction'); Genesis and Jubilees kept; title adjusted

title: A generation of righteousness arises — the plant of righteousness after the destruction
summary_md: Enoch read the whole arc on the heavenly tablets before Noah was weaned: *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1). The child's name carries the first instalment of that promise: *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). The keeping of his seed had already been ordered when the Watchers were sentenced: *And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.’* (1 Enoch 10:3), and in the same breath the planting was named: *Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.* (1 Enoch 10:16). The seed-line of the elect runs through Noah. One house is kept across the judgement, and from it the earth is replanted. The Messiah set his own coming against that same picture: *But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be* (Matthew 24:37), one righteous house preserved while the flood takes all the rest. The generation of righteousness Enoch saw written is not Noah's generation; it is the one that comes when transgression is destroyed for good, and Noah's preserved seed is the line it grows from.
note: 107:6 and 107:9 were invented; built on live 107:1, 107:3, 10:3, 10:16 (10:16 stood); Matthew 24:37 kept; title adjusted

title: Generation upon generation shall transgress — the violence that brings the judgement
summary_md: Before he sends the word down to Lamech, Enoch reads the reason the flood has to come, and it is written as a pattern, not a single crime: *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1). Genesis gives the same verdict over the same earth: *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence* (Genesis 6:11), and the sentence that follows it, *And Elohim (God) said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth* (Genesis 6:13). The flood is not wrath for its own sake. It is the answer to a corruption that had been taught into all flesh, the Watchers' teaching working itself out generation after generation until there was nothing left to spare. Jubilees describes the tide as it rose: *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way... and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth* (Jubilees 5:2). The judgement lands on the corrupting system, and one righteous house is carried through it, which is why the same chapter can name the child: *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). Transgression runs on until the generation of righteousness arises. The flood was the first clearing of the ground for it; the last one is still ahead.
note: 107:8 was invented; built on the live 107:1 and 107:3; Genesis 6 and Jubilees 5:2 kept; title adjusted

title: He called the name of that son Noah — comfort after the destruction, comfort for the cursed ground
summary_md: Enoch's reply reaches Lamech through Methuselah, and the fear over the strange child turns into a name: *And now, my son, go and make known to thy son Lamech that this son, which has been born, is in truth his son, and that (this) is no lie.’* (1 Enoch 107:2), *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). Genesis has Lamech give the name, and gives the reason in his own mouth: *And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which Yahuah (LORD) hath cursed* (Genesis 5:29). Jubilees keeps the same words: *and he called his name Noah, saying, 'This one will comfort me for my trouble and all my work, and for the ground which Yahuah (God) has cursed'* (Jubilees 4:28). Enoch looks forward to the comfort that comes after the destruction; Lamech feels the curse on the ground he is working now; both reasons hang on the one name, and both are right. The seed kept through the flood is also the comfort of the cursed ground, and Hebrews names what that one house did for the rest of the world by being kept: *By faith Noah, being warned of Elohim (God) of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith* (Hebrews 11:7). The comfort was in the child before the flood came, and the name said so.
note: 107:10 was invented; live 107:2-3 has Methuselah naming Noah 'for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction', set beside Genesis 5:29 / Jubilees 4:28 (Lamech's reason) and Hebrews 11:7, all kept; title adjusted

title: Those born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous are resplendent
summary_md: The last page of the book shows the two ends at the same moment, and it is the Father himself speaking: *And now I will summon the spirits of the good who belong to the generation of light, and I will transform those who were born in darkness, who in the flesh were not recompensed with such honour as their faithfulness deserved.* (1 Enoch 108:11), *And I will bring forth in shining light those who have loved My holy name, and I will seat each on the throne of his honour.* (1 Enoch 108:12), *And they shall be resplendent for times without number; for righteousness is the judgement of Elohim (God); for to the faithful He will give faithfulness in the habitation of upright paths.* (1 Enoch 108:13). Then the other side of it: *And they shall see those who were born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous shall be resplendent.* (1 Enoch 108:14), *And the sinners shall cry aloud and see them resplendent, and they indeed will go where days and seasons are prescribed for them.’* (1 Enoch 108:15). The place they go to was shown to Enoch a few verses earlier: *And he said unto me: ‘This place which thou seest—here are cast the spirits of sinners and blasphemers, and of those who work wickedness, and of those who pervert everything that Yahuah (Lord) hath spoken through the mouth of the prophets—(even) the things that shall be.* (1 Enoch 108:6). That is the canon's own last picture: *they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched* (Isaiah 66:24), the verse Yahusha (Jesus) pressed three times. The parable of the tares has the same two halves in the same order, *And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth* (Matthew 13:42), and then, *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father* (Matthew 13:43). The sinners see the righteous resplendent and cry aloud. They were not condemned for being born; they were sent where they had chosen to go, the ones who perverted everything spoken through the prophets, and righteousness is the judgement that sends them.
note: 108:11-13 quoted from the corrupt text (the woes live at 100:7/100:9) and 104:6 invented; rebuilt on the live anchor 108:11-15 with 108:6; Isaiah 66:24, Matthew 13:42-43 kept; new title

title: The two ways — the good keep the law to the end
summary_md: The closing book names its readers in its first line, and they are the keepers of the law: *Another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him, and keep the law in the last days.* (1 Enoch 108:1), *Ye who have done good shall wait for those days till an end is made of those who work evil, and an end of the might of the transgressors.* (1 Enoch 108:2). That is the two ways of the whole Epistle, the same choice set down once at Sinai's gate: *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The good keep the law and wait while an end is made of the transgressors, because the Torah is the way of life and never the curse. The other half of the page describes what the good did not love: *Who love Elohim (God) and loved neither gold nor silver nor any of the good things which are in the world, but gave over their bodies to torture.* (1 Enoch 108:8), *And all the blessings destined for them I have recounted in the books. And He hath assigned them their recompense, because they have been found to be such as loved heaven more than their life in the world, and though they were trodden under foot of wicked men, and experienced abuse and reviling from them and were put to shame, yet they blessed Me.* (1 Enoch 108:10). The ones who trod them under foot are the hoarders James names plainly: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1), *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days* (James 5:3). Isaiah pronounces the same woe on the systems that swallow the land: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place* (Isaiah 5:8). The two ways divide the keeper of the law, who loved heaven more than his life, from the oppressor whose gold burns him.
note: CHECK: 108:16 and 108:10 quotes were invented (ch 108 has 15 verses); re-quoted 108:1-2 in full and set 108:8 / 108:10 (live) in place of the invented riches lines; Deut 30:19, James, Isaiah kept

title: The cherub and the flaming sword at the eastern gate
summary_md: Adam and Eve, blind with sorrow, climb the border of the garden until they stand at the gate they may no longer enter: *And the cherub who guarded the garden was standing at the western gate, and guarding it against Adam and Eve, lest they should suddenly come into the garden* (1-adam-eve 54:3); *suddenly came the cherub with a flashing sword of fire in his hand* (1-adam-eve 54:4). This is the very scene Moses sealed at the close of Eden: *Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken* (Genesis 3:23), and *he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24). Jubilees keeps the same memory of the sending-forth: *And He made for them coats of skin, and clothed them, and sent them forth from the Garden of Eden* (Jubilees 3:26). Enoch was carried to the same garden and shown the tree that put them outside it, and the angel told him whose parents had eaten from it: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). From the first day outside the garden the way to life is guarded, and it stays guarded until the Lamb opens it again: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14).
note: 32:4 'tree of life' quote was invented (32:4 is the tree of wisdom); the live 32:6 names Adam and Eve eating and driven out, which is the thread's own scene; rest kept verbatim

title: I saw Yahuah on his throne, and all the host of heaven
summary_md: Micaiah lifts the veil on the heavenly court: *Hear thou therefore the word of Yahuah (LORD): I saw Yahuah (LORD) sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left* (1 Kings 22:19). This is Yahuah (God) enthroned amid the divine council, the Most High on his throne, the host of heaven his ministers and witnesses, deliberating over the fall of Ahab. It is the same court the other seers are shown. Job sees it: *Now there was a day when the sons of Elohim (God) came to present themselves before Yahuah (LORD)* (Job 1:6). Daniel beholds the enthroned Most High in fire: *the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow... his throne was like the fiery flame* (Daniel 7:9), attended by the innumerable host — *thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set* (Daniel 7:10). Isaiah's call is word for word Micaiah's sight: *I saw also Yahuah (Lord) sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple* (Isaiah 6:1). And John on Patmos hears the same numberless company — *the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands* (Revelation 5:11) — round about the throne. Enoch is carried up into the same house and sees the same throne with the same host before it: *And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim.* (1 Enoch 14:18), *And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow.* (1 Enoch 14:20), *The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.* (1 Enoch 14:22). One throne, one Most High, one host of heaven encircling him in counsel and in worship. This is not a co-equal trinity and not an Arian counterfeit either: the Father is the enthroned Most High, and the host, including the spirit who comes forth and *stood before Yahuah* (22:21), stand before him as servants who do his bidding.
note: CHECK: the mechanical re-quote had swapped the throne for 18:8 (a mountain 'like the throne'); the throne vision is live 14:18-22, quoted there (14:22's ten thousand times ten thousand matches Daniel 7:10); rest kept

title: The spirits in prison — the days of Noah — the Watchers (Genesis 6, 1 Enoch, Jubilees, Jude)
summary_md: Here is the showcase weave of the epistle. *For Messiah (Christ) also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to Elohim (God), being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of Elohim (God) waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water* (1 Peter 3:18-20). The *spirits in prison* who *were disobedient... in the days of Noah* are the fallen ones of Genesis 6: *the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose* (Genesis 6:2), and *there were giants in the earth in those days* (Genesis 6:4), so that *the wickedness of man was great in the earth* (Genesis 6:5) and the longsuffering of Yahuah (LORD) waited while Noah built. The Hebrew library narrates the imprisonment Peter assumes. Yahuah (God) commands Raphael, *Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness* (1 Enoch 10:4), and Michael to bind Semjaza and his associates: *bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement* (1 Enoch 10:12), *to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever* (1 Enoch 10:13). Enoch the scribe is sent to *declare to the Watchers of the heaven who have left the high heaven... and have taken unto themselves wives* (1 Enoch 12:4), saying *Azâzêl, thou shalt have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against thee to put thee in bonds* (1 Enoch 13:1) — the pattern of a righteous one sent to proclaim to the bound spirits. Enoch is shown the place itself: *The angel said: ‘This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven. And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.* (1 Enoch 18:14-15), *And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’* (1 Enoch 18:16), and the angel says plainly of it, *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Jubilees tells the same days: *the angels of Elohim (God)... took themselves wives of all whom they chose, and they bare to them sons and they were giants* (Jubilees 5:1); Yahuah (God) *bade us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and behold they are bound* (Jubilees 5:6), *bound in the depths of the earth for ever, until the day of the great condemnation* (Jubilees 5:10). The apostolic witnesses confirm the one narrative: *the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 6), and *Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). One story runs from Genesis 6 through 1 Enoch and Jubilees to Jude, 2 Peter, and here: the Watchers, the giants, the Flood, the prison of bound spirits reserved unto judgement. Keep the order Peter keeps: it is the Son, *put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit,* who *went and preached unto the spirits in prison.* The Son is the one put to death and made alive again and sent to proclaim; the Father is the one who quickens and raises him — *the resurrection of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (1 Peter 3:21) — and exalts him to his right hand (1 Peter 3:22). The proclamation to the imprisoned spirits is no rescue of the rebel angels but the announcement of the sentence already gone forth, the same *no peace* Enoch carried to the bound Watchers of old.

title: The earth gives back her dead: the day of resurrection in the Hebrew library (2 Esdras 7, 1 Enoch 51)
summary_md: The hope Paul preached — *the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first* (1 Thessalonians 4:16) — the restored library held before him, beholding the earth and the grave surrendering the asleep. The seer of Esdras saw it: *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them* (2 Esdras 7:32). And Enoch beheld the same: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes.* (1 Enoch 51:1), *And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:2), *For in those days the Elect One shall arise, And the earth shall rejoice, And the righteous shall dwell upon it, And the elect shall walk thereon.* (1 Enoch 51:5). The earth restoring the asleep, Sheol giving back what it received, the righteous chosen out from among them at the arising of the Elect One — this is *Yahuah (Lord) himself shall descend from heaven... and the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first.* The hope is one; the risings are two. At his coming the dead in Messiah (Christ) rise first — the righteous seed out of Sheol, the first resurrection, that the chosen should be saved. After the reign the earth gives up the rest of her dead to the judgment of the dead, the great resurrection. Not a secret snatching severed from the people, but the asleep raised each in their own order.

title: Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day (Isaiah 60, 1 Enoch 58)
summary_md: *Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness* (1 Thessalonians 5:5). Against the day of darkness that overtakes the sleeping, Paul sets the assembly on the day-side of the great division — and that division is Isaiah's. *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee* (Isaiah 60:1); and the contrast: *For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but Yahuah (LORD) shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee* (Isaiah 60:2). While gross darkness covers the peoples, Yahuah (LORD) rises upon his own — and those upon whom his glory is seen are the children of light, the children of the day. Enoch's third Parable holds the same hope for the same people: *And the righteous shall be in the light of the sun, And the elect in the light of eternal life: The days of their life shall be unending, And the days of the holy without number.* (1 Enoch 58:3), for in the end *And there shall be a light that never endeth, And to a limit (lit. ‘number’) of days they shall not come, For the darkness shall first have been destroyed, [And the light established before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits] And the light of uprightness established for ever before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 58:6), because, as the same Parable says, *it has become bright as the sun upon earth, And the darkness is past.* (1 Enoch 58:5). The portion of the elect is unceasing light; the night is destroyed. So Paul reasons from the assembly's identity to its conduct: *Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober* (1 Thessalonians 5:6), *For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night* (1 Thessalonians 5:7). Sleep and drunkenness belong to the night; watchfulness and sobriety to the day. Because the glory of Yahuah (LORD) has risen upon them, the children of the day are not overtaken by the day of darkness.

title: The western gates — the sun draws away its light, the days of the year
summary_md: At the western parts Enoch is shown gates *corresponding to the eastern gates, opposite to where the sun sets, according to the number of the days* of the year (2 Enoch 14:1), where the sun *goes down to the western gates, and draws away its light... under the earth* (2 Enoch 14:2). It ain't new — the lights were appointed *for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), and the Psalmist already traced the sun's full arc: *His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it* (Psalms 19:6). Enoch's own Astronomical Book had marked the same setting: *And this is the first law of the luminaries: the luminary the Sun has its rising in the eastern portals of the heaven, and its setting in the western portals of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 72:2), *When the sun rises in the heaven, he comes forth through that fourth portal thirty mornings in succession, and sets accurately in the fourth portal in the west of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 72:8). The sun's evening descent and the counted days of the year are the ordered courses Yahuah set, not a secret of the seer's own making.

title: The solar year and the lunar year — the ordinances of the lights
summary_md: Enoch is shown the two reckonings side by side: the moon *accomplishes the three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter days of the solar year, while the lunar year has three hundred fifty-four, and there are wanting to it twelve days* (2 Enoch 16:3), with longer cycles closing the gap. It ain't new — the sun and moon keep distinct ordinances by Yahuah's appointment: *which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night* (Jeremiah 31:35). Enoch's own Astronomical Book had weighed the same difference, and it counts the moon's shortfall against the sun's 364: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12), *And the overplus of the sun and of the stars amounts to six days: in 5 years 6 days every year come to 30 days: and the moon falls behind the sun and stars to the number of 30 days.* (1 Enoch 74:11), *For the moon alone the days amount in 3 years to 1,062 days, and in 5 years she falls 50 days behind: [i.e. to the sum (of 1,770) there is to be added (1,000 and) 62 days.]* (1 Enoch 74:14). Jubilees warns of the lunar drift: *now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon* (Jubilees 6:36) — the same falling-behind Enoch counted. The lights keep their separate counts by ordinance, not by chance.

title: The courses of the moon — the lesser light for seasons
summary_md: Now the moon's turn: *the other course, that of the moon, twelve great gates, crowned from west to east, by which the moon goes in and out of the customary times* (2 Enoch 16:1), reckoned out month by month through its gates. It ain't new — the moon is the lesser light Moses records, *the lesser light to rule the night* (Genesis 1:16), and the Psalmist's appointed timekeeper: *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down* (Psalms 104:19). Enoch's own Astronomical Book had already traced the moon through the same portals: *And I saw another course, a law for her, (and) how according to that law she performs her monthly revolution.* (1 Enoch 74:1), *In single seventh parts she accomplishes all her light in the east, and in single seventh parts accomplishes all her darkness in the west.* (1 Enoch 74:3). The moon's circuit through its gates is not augury; it is the lesser light keeping its appointed seasons as Moses and the Psalms declare.

title: A later generation that reads the books and tells the next
summary_md: Beyond the flood the Lord promises a faithful remnant who will recover the written witness: *Behold from their seed shall arise another generation... He who raises that generation, shall reveal to them the books of your handwriting, of your fathers... to the faithful men and workers of my pleasure* (2 Enoch 35:1-2), *And they shall tell another generation, and those others having read shall be glorified thereafter* (2 Enoch 35:3). It ain't new — this is the very charge of the law, that the witness be written and handed on: *That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children* (Psalms 78:6), *We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalms 78:4). Enoch himself was given this commission in his own book, with a year to carry it out: *And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: ‘Declare everything to thy son Methuselah, and show to all thy children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), for He is their Creator.* (1 Enoch 81:5), *One year we will leave thee with thy son, till thou givest thy (last) commands, that thou mayst teach thy children and record (it) for them, and testify to all thy children; and in the second year they shall take thee from their midst.* (1 Enoch 81:6). The handing-down of the books is the handing-down Moses and the prophets command.

title: No other Elohim but me — teach and keep the commandments
summary_md: Enoch is sent back for thirty days with a single charge for his house: *tell your sons and all your household... how there is no other Elohim (God) but me. And that they may always keep my commandments, and begin to read and take in the books of your handwriting* (2 Enoch 36:1-2). It ain't new — this is the Shema and its commission word for word: *Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD)* (Deuteronomy 6:4), and *these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house* (Deuteronomy 6:6-7). The charge to teach the sons is the one the holy ones laid on Enoch at his own door: *One year we will leave thee with thy son, till thou givest thy (last) commands, that thou mayst teach thy children and record (it) for them, and testify to all thy children; and in the second year they shall take thee from their midst.* (1 Enoch 81:6). 2 Enoch teaches no new God and no new law — only the One and His commandments, handed to the sons.

title: The prisoners in pain and all that are judged — written down
summary_md: Enoch's books reach past the lights to the place of sentence: *I saw how the prisoners are in pain, expecting the limitless judgment. And I wrote down all those being judged by the judge, and all their judgment and sentences and all their works* (2 Enoch 40:10-11). It ain't new — this is the bound waiting for judgment Peter and Jude name: *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). And the writing-down of every work for the judgment is the books of remembrance the prophets keep — what Enoch was charged to record in his own book: *And he said unto me: ‘Observe, Enoch, these heavenly tablets, And read what is written thereon, And mark every individual fact.’* (1 Enoch 81:1), *And I observed the heavenly tablets, and read everything which was written (thereon) and understood everything, and read the book of all the deeds of mankind, and of all the children of flesh that shall be upon the earth to the remotest generations.* (1 Enoch 81:2). Enoch's ledger of works and sentences is the very ledger the judgment opens.

title: The angels that sinned in chains of darkness, Noah, and Sodom — the Watchers (Genesis 6, 1 Enoch, Jubilees, Jude)
summary_md: To prove the certain judgment of the false teachers, Kepha (Peter) lays down three judgments the library records — and the first of them is the one the whole library keeps coming back to: *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment; And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample... And delivered just Lot* (2 Peter 2:4-7). The *angels that sinned* are the Watchers — the *sons of Elohim (God)* who *came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them... men of renown* (Genesis 6:4). Kepha is not coining a myth; he is reading Torah's own account of the fall that brought the Flood, and the library tells exactly how those angels were bound. Yahuah (God) commanded, *Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness* (1 Enoch 10:4), and of Semjâzâ, *bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement* (1 Enoch 10:12) — the very *chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.* Enoch was shown the place itself: *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Jubilees agrees to the word: Elohim (God) *bade us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and behold they are bound* (Jubilees 5:6), *bound in the depths of the earth for ever, until the day of the great condemnation* (Jubilees 5:10). This is the same Watchers record Kepha (Peter) leaned on in his first letter (1 Peter 3:19-20) and Jude leans on in his: *the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 6). Then the Flood: *Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark* (Genesis 7:23), *Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations* (Genesis 6:9) — *Noah the eighth person,* the few *saved by water* (1 Peter 3:20), the days of Noah the Master made the type of his coming (Matthew 24:37). Then Sodom: *Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire... and he overthrew those cities* (Genesis 19:24-25), *set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire* (Jude 7); and just Lot delivered when *they brought him forth, and set him without the city* (Genesis 19:16). The Hebrew library catalogues every one of these: *the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it... in a piece of wood* (Wisdom 10:4), *she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities* (Wisdom 10:6), and in the same order Kepha keeps — *the old giants, who fell away* (Sirach 16:7), the place of Lot not spared (Sirach 16:8), Noah *left as a remnant to the earth, when the flood came* (Sirach 44:17). The lesson is one: *Yahuah (Lord) knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished* (2 Peter 2:9). The angels that sinned, the old world, the cities of the plain — the judgment-history the whole library records, and the false teachers stand in its line.
